title: Why React is a library where Angular is a framework, and what you assemble yourself

videos.script:
React is the name you will see in most front-end job adverts. {{library}} It is also smaller than most people expect. It does one job: it turns what your app knows into what the screen shows, and keeps the two in step.

{{assemble}} Everything else, you choose. Which address shows which screen. How data arrives from a server. How a form checks what was typed. Angular ships all of that in one box. React ships none of it, and this lesson lists what you will add, and in which lesson.

{{setup}} Then your computer. If you took the JavaScript course, Node is already there, and you will only check that it answers. {{project}} You will create the project with one command, and pin every version, so that your app and the one in these transcripts are made of the same code.

{{look}} You will also build a small tool that reads a page as text, the way a screen reader would. That is how this course shows you a page without a screenshot.

{{planner}} And you will meet the app. A study planner, with two screens and one small file of data. The Angular, Vue and Svelte courses build the same one, and the last lesson puts them side by side.
